title: Design System: Manan Bhullar Real Estate

display.purpose: Hero/subhero h1 only, white on dark backgrounds.

body.purpose: Running paragraph text, ink or ink-soft.

shadows.name: floating-overlay
shadows.purpose: Reserved for genuinely floating UI (tooltips, dropdowns, mobile menu) -- not a general card style.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid accent-fill CTA. Used for the lowest-friction contact action (form, text) per this session's CTA-hierarchy fix.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: #1E5FD9; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 14px 24px; text-decoration: none; border: none; border-radius: 0; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #164FB8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #1E5FD9; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Outline Button (on dark)
components.description: Secondary action on a dark section. Used for the higher-friction contact action (phone call) per the CTA-hierarchy fix.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: transparent; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 14px 24px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.5); border-radius: 0; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); }

components.name: Eyebrow Badge (light)
components.description: Small uppercase label above a heading. Light-mode default -- was missing as a base rule before this session, rendering invisibly outside the hero.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { display: inline-block; font-family: 'General Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #E4E2DD; color: #4A4A4A; padding: 7px 14px; }

components.name: Eyebrow Badge (dark)
components.description: Eyebrow badge variant for dark/hero sections.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow-dark { display: inline-block; font-family: 'General Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.02em; text-transform: uppercase; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.18); color: #fff; padding: 7px 14px; }

components.name: Simple Card
components.description: Sharp-cornered content card with hairline border, no shadow.
components.html: Buy a HomeFull buyer representation, from search to keys in hand.
components.css: .ds-card { display: block; border: 1px solid #E4E2DD; background: #FFFFFF; padding: 24px; border-radius: 0; text-decoration: none; color: #121212; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #1E5FD9; } .ds-card strong { display: block; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card span { display: block; font-size: 0.86rem; color: #4A4A4A; line-height: 1.55; }

components.name: Form Field + Trust Line
components.description: Lead-capture form input styling plus the credential trust line added under the heading this session.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-form { background: #FFFFFF; padding: 36px; border: 1px solid #E4E2DD; } .ds-form h3 { font-size: 1.2rem; margin: 0 0 6px; } .ds-form-trust { font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; color: #164FB8; margin: 0 0 20px; letter-spacing: 0.01em; } .ds-input { width: 100%; border: 1px solid #E4E2DD; padding: 12px 14px; font-family: 'General Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; background: #FAFAF8; color: #121212; border-radius: 0; }

narrative.overview: This is a site built to read like a well-organized, trustworthy briefing document, not a sales brochure. Off-white paper, near-black ink, a single confident blue used sparingly, and sharp, undecorated rectangles throughout -- the visual system gets out of the way of the facts. Every corner on the site is a hard 90 degrees; there is no radius token in use anywhere in the codebase, and that is deliberate, not an oversight. The palette was explicitly pared down from an earlier two-tone red/blue, warm/cool scheme the client found busy, and a later pitch for a SaaS-style dark navy/indigo/gold identity was proposed and declined. Dark sections (hero, nav, footer, closing CTAs) alternate with light and raised sections through every page for rhythm -- a page that stays one shade for its whole length is a defect, not a style.
keyCharacteristics: One accent blue, used deliberately and sparingly
Hard, sharp corners everywhere -- no border-radius anywhere in the stylesheet
Off-white paper over pure white for body backgrounds
Alternating light/raised/dark section rhythm down every page
One typeface (General Sans) for everything, no monospace anywhere
Custom blue SVG line icons, never emoji

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only hue on the site besides neutrals. It was chosen after two more colorful alternatives were built and rejected by the client as too busy.

rules.name: The Off-White Rule
rules.body: Page backgrounds are --paper (#FAFAF8), never pure white. Pure white (--paper-raised) is reserved for elements that need to visually lift off the page.

rules.name: The No-Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono was fully removed site-wide per explicit client request. Never reach for a monospace font on any new UI element, however digit-heavy.

rules.name: The Sharp Corner Rule
rules.body: Do not add border-radius to any new component. The absence of rounding is a confirmed, site-wide visual choice, not an inconsistency to fix.

rules.name: The Flat-Card Rule
rules.body: Cards and content boxes are distinguished by a hairline border and/or background shift, not a shadow. Reserve box-shadow for genuinely floating UI.

dos: Do keep every new section's background alternating with its neighbors rather than letting two-plus sections in a row share the same background.
Do use the Eyebrow Badge's light-mode default on any plain or raised section, and only reach for the dark override inside an actual dark-background section.
Do make the lowest-friction contact action (text/form) the visually primary button, and the highest-friction one (phone call) secondary.
Do use the established SVG icon set and its blue/line-icon convention for any new icon need.
donts: Don't add border-radius to any element.
Don't introduce a second accent hue.
Don't reach for a monospace font for any digit-heavy content.
Don't add a drop-shadow-based card style as a general pattern.
Don't use emoji as UI icons.
